value_text: In a 198-site survey, 69 sites had brown trout only, 63 had G. vulgaris only, and only 9 had both species.
relevance_to_pedder: Strong comparative evidence that brown trout can fragment non-diadromous galaxiid distributions.
notes: Updated from review-level extraction to the direct primary paper.

value_text: Galaxiids were mostly found above trout-blocking waterfalls, and trout absence, not land-use degradation, best predicted galaxiid presence and abundance.
source_locator: Townsend and Crowl 1991, discussion and waterfall results
relevance_to_pedder: Supports treating trout pressure as a plausible primary driver rather than a coincidental correlate of degraded habitat.
notes: The paper explicitly favors predation as the most likely mechanism and shows the importance of trout-blocking waterfalls.

value_text: The review states brown trout feed on a wide range of organisms including crustaceans, insects, molluscs and small fish.
relevance_to_pedder: Useful prior support for size-structured predation pressure by trout on small native fish.

value_text: Brook trout in Australia are restricted to Tasmania and New South Wales, tend to move into small tributaries, and feed on aquatic crustaceans, insects, molluscs and small fish.
relevance_to_pedder: Relevant mainly for later Clarence Lagoon work, especially brook trout diet and tributary use.

salmonid_or_competitor: juvenile brown trout and rainbow trout
value_text: Glova and Sagar found that G. brevipinnis fed almost exclusively at night and used somewhat faster water than juvenile trout, so overlap in food and space was real but partly reduced by diel and microhabitat partitioning.
relevance_to_pedder: Useful proxy for coexistence under juvenile-trout conditions, but also a reminder that reduced overlap does not imply no interaction.
notes: Best interpreted as a juvenile-trout coexistence case rather than a mature-trout safety signal.

value_text: Ault and White showed that after quantitatively accounting for habitat structure, brown trout still explained substantially lower densities of G. truttaceus in Tasmanian streams.
relevance_to_pedder: High-value Tasmanian proxy for trout-galaxiid interaction strengths in another native galaxiid.
notes: Direct primary source now available locally; useful against a habitat-confounding objection.

value_text: Chilcott et al. cite Arthington (1991) on ecological and genetic impacts of introduced and translocated freshwater fishes in Australia.
relevance_to_pedder: Potential review source for generic prior ranges and broader risk framing.

source_locator: ALA species search and occurrence APIs, queried 2026-03-23
relevance_to_pedder: Useful for expanding from narrative evidence into specimen-backed comparative occurrence data.
notes: Requires careful post-query filtering because locality strings and record types are heterogeneous.

value_text: Ault and White found that larger G. truttaceus shifted into deeper, cover-rich, slow-flowing habitat, but trout presence still depressed abundance beyond what habitat alone predicted.
source_locator: Ault and White 1994, abstract and recovered discussion
relevance_to_pedder: Supports modeling trout effects as partly mediated by habitat refuge quality rather than as a uniform pressure.

value_text: Glova and Sagar concluded that coexistence with salmonids depended strongly on trout size structure and substrate cover, with predation becoming more important where older trout were present and bottom cover was limited.
relevance_to_pedder: Useful for the transient-overshoot idea because it highlights the special risk posed by larger trout and reduced cover.

salmonid_or_competitor: introduced salmonids and other introduced fish
value_text: Hardie et al. identify exotic species, especially salmonids, as the key current threat class for Tasmanian galaxiids and argue that coexistence with introduced salmonids should be examined explicitly rather than assumed.
source_locator: Hardie et al. 2006, abstract and threat discussion
relevance_to_pedder: Strong Tasmania-wide framing source for the Introduction and for justifying comparative priors.

value_text: McDowall argues that across southern cool-temperate systems, salmonid introductions have repeatedly caused major galaxioid declines and often left communities with little direct co-occurrence evidence because displacement and predation have already broken the original overlap.
relevance_to_pedder: Useful high-level synthesis for framing Pedder as part of a broader recurrent pattern, while still leaving room for local contingency.

value_text: Jense et al. found that contemporary genetic isolation in G. johnstoni is better explained by habitat preferences and post-glacial recolonisation than by brown trout invasion alone.
source_locator: Jense et al. 2025, abstract and discussion
relevance_to_pedder: Important framing control-case showing that present-day trout allopatry is not, by itself, proof of trout-caused fragmentation.

value_text: Waters et al. show that contemporary distributions do not always predict introgression history and argue that recent anthropogenic fragmentation, including salmonid-driven range loss, can obscure past contact among galaxiid lineages.
source_locator: Waters et al. 2023, abstract and introduction
relevance_to_pedder: Useful genetics-side warning against reading hybridization history directly from present-day spatial separation.
